item.title: How Parliaments Polarize: Legislative Replacement and Adaptation in Chile
item.description: The growing polarization of political elites is usually interpreted as the result of a progressive radicalization of their members. However, a parliament can also become more polarized without its members substantially changing their positions, simply because incoming legislators are more extreme than those they replace. Distinguishing between these two mechanisms is key to understanding how political representation changes over time. The project is carried out by Jorge Fábrega. Data and methodology The project analyzes roll-call votes in Chile’s Chamber of Deputies over six legislative periods, from 2002 to 2026.
